subject: general
question: Complement of an angle is 12° more than twice the angle. Find the angle.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of an angle and its complement is always 90°.

Angle + (2 × Angle + 12°) = 90°

3 × Angle = 90° − 12° = 78°

Angle = 78° ÷ 3 = 26°

**∴ The correct option is (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Complement of angle = 2 × Angle + 12°

**Formula Used:**

Angle + Complement = 90°

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the required angle be x.

⇒ Its complement = 90° − x.

⇒ According to the question: 90° − x = 2x + 12°

⇒ 90° − 12° = 2x + x

⇒ 78° = 3x

⇒ x = 78° ÷ 3

⇒ x = 26°

**∴ The correct option is (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles

Two angles are called complementary if their sum is exactly 90°.

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are called supplementary if their sum is exactly 180°.

Linear Pair

A pair of adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines that sum to 180°.

Reflex Angle

An angle which is greater than 180° but less than 360°.
